pages.text: Their teacher took the class to the school garden for a bug hunt. “Look, but do not touch,” she said. “We keep our hands away from animals we do not know. We look gently and put everything back.”
sentences: Their teacher took the class to the school garden for a bug hunt.
“Look, but do not touch,” she said.
“We keep our hands away from animals we do not know.
We look gently and put everything back.”
pages.alt: At the leafy edge of a Ghanaian school garden, Tuffour with a magnifying glass and Atiah with a sketchbook listen to their teacher.

pages.text: Under a damp log, Tuffour saw a worm and some small insects. “It is cool and wet here,” said Atiah. “They like damp places.” They sketched it in their book. Then they put the log back as they found it.
sentences: Under a damp log, Tuffour saw a worm and some small insects.

pages.alt: Crouching at a safe distance beside a lifted damp wooden log, Tuffour and Atiah observe an earthworm and tiny beetles on dark moist soil.

pages.text: Near the water tap, there was a small frog. It sat in a wet patch among the leaves. “Frogs need water,” said the teacher, “so they stay near wet places.”
sentences: Near the water tap, there was a small frog.
It sat in a wet patch among the leaves.
“Frogs need water,” said the teacher, “so they stay near wet places.”
pages.alt: Near a dripping outdoor school standpipe tap, a small green-brown frog sits calmly among wet green leaves while Tuffour, Atiah and their teacher watch quietly.

pages.text: On the school wall, a line of ants marched to a small mound of soil. “That is their home,” said Atiah. “It keeps them safe.” At the top of the tree, a bird sat on a nest.
sentences: On the school wall, a line of ants marched to a small mound of soil.
“That is their home,” said Atiah.
“It keeps them safe.” At the top of the tree, a bird sat on a nest.
pages.alt: By the low school wall, a neat line of ants marches to a small soil mound while high in a leafy garden tree a yellow weaver bird sits on its woven nest.

pages.text: “Each of these animals has a habitat,” said the teacher. “A habitat is the place where a living thing finds food, water and shelter. A worm’s habitat is the damp soil. A bird’s habitat is a tree.”
sentences: “Each of these animals has a habitat,” said the teacher.
“A habitat is the place where a living thing finds food, water and shelter.
A worm’s habitat is the damp soil.
A bird’s habitat is a tree.”
pages.alt: Under the garden shade, the teacher holds up a picture board with four wordless drawings showing a worm in soil, a frog by water, ants at a mound and a bird in a tree.

pages.text: Back in class, they drew pictures matching each animal to where they found it. “If we cut down the tree or take the log away for good,” said Tuffour, “the animals lose their home.” The class agreed to look after the garden, and washed their hands.

pages.alt: Outside the classroom, Tuffour and Atiah wash their hands with soap at a Veronica bucket while classmates place wordless animal-and-home drawings on a table.

activities.question: Why do frogs stay near wet places?
What is a habitat?
options: The place where a living thing finds food, water and shelter

activities.prompt: Put the bug hunt in order.
items: Find a frog near the tap.
See ants and a bird’s nest.
Match each animal to its habitat.

activities.definition: The place where a living thing finds food, water and shelter.

glossary.definition: The place where a living thing finds food, water and shelter.
A place that keeps a living thing safe from weather and enemies.
